moved.sentence: Per GDPR Art. 7 (and similar regimes), consent **MUST** be:

judged.note: The GDPR Art. 7 (and similar regimes) basis is kept in rationale for all four conditions, and each condition is its own MUST rule starting with must-be-freely-given.

moved.sentence: **Freely given**: not bundled with service access; refusal **MUST NOT** degrade core functionality that does not depend on the processing.

judged.note: Freely given is kept at MUST: not bundled with service access, and refusal MUST NOT degrade core functionality that does not depend on the processing.

moved.sentence: **Specific and granular**: each distinct purpose (analytics, marketing, personalization, third-party sharing) **MUST** have its own toggle.

judged.note: Specific and granular is kept at MUST, with its own toggle per distinct purpose and the same four example purposes.

moved.sentence: **Informed**: present the purpose, controller identity, data categories, and the right to withdraw before capture.

judged.note: Informed is kept at MUST: purpose, controller identity, data categories and right to withdraw presented before capture.

moved.sentence: **Unambiguous**: require an affirmative action (an explicit opt-in).

judged.note: Unambiguous is kept at MUST: an affirmative action, an explicit opt-in.

moved.sentence: Re-request consent when the purpose changes, a new data category is added, or a new processor is introduced.

judged.note: Re-requesting consent on a purpose change, a new data category or a new processor is kept at SHOULD with all three triggers.

moved.sentence: Set a re-confirmation cadence for long-lived consent (commonly revisited at 12–24 months) per applicable guidance and risk.

judged.note: A re-confirmation cadence for long-lived consent, commonly 12-24 months, per applicable guidance and risk, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: This is engineering guidance for building consent flows, not legal advice — confirm obligations with counsel for each jurisdiction.

judged.note: The engineering-not-legal-advice disclaimer and confirming obligations with counsel for each jurisdiction are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Persist each decision as an **append-only, immutable** record.

judged.note: Persisting each decision as an append-only, immutable record is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Store the exact consent-notice text or a content hash so you can prove what the user saw.

judged.note: Storing the exact notice text or a content hash, with the reason of proving what the user saw, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Pin the policy to a dated, versioned revision.

judged.note: Pinning the policy to a dated, versioned revision is kept at SHOULD.
